title: Nine Notes of Paper
subtitle: 现金与支付 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 现金与支付（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：现金与支付（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：cash　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cash 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my mother was sent to count ① cash she could not change, and she said the changing was the whole of the lesson. The ② cash, meaning the notes and not the account, was nine notes and was counted by whoever came last; cash, she said, is the only thing in a till that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cash in that till had the same crease, and the ④ cash at the front, meaning the one the shopman kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. Cash, my grandmother said, is nine parts paper and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the paper is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cash was the whole of the money, meaning the wealth it stood for and not the notes. The ⑥ cash, meaning the wealth and not any of that, is the only thing in a market that everybody asks for and nobody questions; cash, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both notes and wealth. She said the wealth is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ cash had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the crease. The ⑧ cash of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine notes and eleven years of counting; cash, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cash I remember is the one at the front, which was paid in 1978 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ sum of cash, my grandmother said in 1983, is the only thing that improves by being spent; every cash, she said, is wealth that has agreed to look like notes. She said the wealth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 现金（指那些纸币本身，与账户相对）
C. 固定搭配：count cash 清点现金
D. n. 现金（指钱柜里每一沓）
E. n. 现金（指前面那一沓）
F. n. 现款；财富（抽象：与那些纸币相对）
G. n. 那份财富（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The cash, meaning the notes and not the account
cash was the whole of the money
the cash had become a number in a report
The cash of the whole thing
A sum of cash, my grandmother said in 1983

answers.why: count cash 意为“清点现金”，1958 年母亲被派去清点她换不开的现金。
cash 意为“现金”，指那些纸币本身而不是账户，共九张，由最后走的人清点。
cash 指钱柜里每一沓现金，每一沓都是同样的折痕。
cash 指前面那一沓（店主留的那一沓），是唯一有人认真清点过的。
cash 意为“现款、财富”，与那些纸币相对，父亲说 cash 就是那笔钱的全部。
cash 为抽象用法，指那份财富本身，是市场上人人都索要、却没人质疑的东西。
cash 意为“现金、现款”，到 1973 年这笔 cash 成了报告里的一个数字。
cash 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九张纸币和十一年的清点。
cash 意为“现金”，我记得的是前面那一沓，1978 年付出，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
cash 为抽象总称，祖母说一笔现金是唯一会因为被花出去而变好的东西。

answers: In 1958 my mother was sent to count cash she could not change, and she said the changing was the whole of the lesson.
The cash, meaning the notes and not the account, was nine notes and was counted by whoever came last.
Every cash in that till had the same crease.
The cash at the front, meaning the one the shopman kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly.
My father said cash was the whole of the money, meaning the wealth it stood for and not the notes.
